newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer in quiet, thin trading.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer in quiet, thin trading.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer, helped by good demand and shrinking stocks in the United States, traders said.

"Yesterday we saw some profit-taking and we recovered today. The COMEX stocks went down and that helped," Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said. "Demand for copper is good and we are seeing a move to 110.00 cents."
COMEX stocks have tumbled sharply in the last two days, down a combined 4,260 short tons to 25,748 tons on Monday and Tuesday.
The LME backwardation remained firm at $173/$177, recovering from a slight dip earlier in the session to give continued support to the market, traders said.
March COMEX settled 1.45 cents firmer at 106.90 cents per pound, traded 107.00 to 105.10 cents. Spot January went out 1.20 cents higher at 109.40 cents.
Volume was moderate at an estimated 6,500 lots compared to Tuesday's official 8,413 lots.
Activity in copper was fairly muted because much of the base metals complex's focus was on zinc which hit a 23-month high for LME three months.
